Yes, `Executor.map` accepts `buffersize` in this snapshot, and its default is `None`.

```json
{"facts": {"available": "true", "default": "None"}}
```

The v2 documentation gives the signature as `map(fn, *iterables, timeout=None, chunksize=1, buffersize=None)`. When `buffersize` is `None`, the iterables are collected immediately. When it is set, it caps the number of submitted tasks whose results have not yet been yielded.

An earlier Claude Code note ("Executor buffering") said `buffersize` was absent. That contradicts the v2 corpus, so I did not rely on it.
